svg.aria-label: How to write ं: one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing ं
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ं (devanagari), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Static.ttf. Stroke order after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Devanagari recognizer, class 57 (ं, anusvara): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>. Source note on variation: The recognizer stores native writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 156 of the 157 stored prototypes of the anusvara are one pen-down stroke, and 112 of the 157 (71%) turn anticlockwise. Where the small loop starts is less settled: 94 of the 157 (60%) start in its upper half, so the path starts at the top. The printed dot is solid, so the pen path circles inside it. Each sign was written by itself, with no consonant beside it, so the traces fix the sign's own strokes but not when it is written against its consonant or the headline; the book draws the sign alone and composes no Devanagari word from it. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Devanagari outline of the sign on its own. The underlying HP Labs data is licensed for research use only, so only counts and shares are cited here, and no trace was copied. Handwriting varies by writer.
